title: Agrovesto dev — infrastructure
description: Everything the dev stack runs on: the EC2 host, what the containers do to it, and the observability stack watching both. Per-container detail lives on the apps & services dashboard, requests and clients on the traffic dashboard, log lines on the logs dashboard.

panels.title: Logging volume used
panels.description: Loki chunks, Tempo blocks and Prometheus TSDB all live on this volume.

panels.title: CPU by mode
panels.description: iowait climbing while user stays flat means the volume, not the CPU, is the limit.

panels.title: Swap
panels.description: Anything above zero for long means the containers' limits add up to more than the box has.

panels.title: Load average
panels.description: The vCPU line is the reference: load above it means work is queueing.

panels.title: Filesystem usage per mount
panels.description: HostDiskAlmostFull fires on any mount that runs past the free-space threshold in var.alert_rules.

panels.title: Inodes used per mount
panels.description: Loki and Tempo write a lot of small files: inodes can run out before bytes do.

panels.title: What the containers do to the host
Container CPU vs host capacity
panels.description: Both in percent of one core, so the two lines are directly comparable.

panels.title: Sum of the memory limits
panels.description: What docker-compose.yml promises in mem_limit. Overcommit is fine until the working sets grow into it.

panels.title: Sum of the CPU limits
panels.description: The cgroup CPU period is 100000µs on this host, so quota / 100000 is cores.

panels.title: Containers running
panels.description: Every container on the box, including the ones this stack does not manage.

panels.title: Writable layer per container
panels.description: Growth here lands on the root volume; Loki and Tempo write to the logging volume instead.

panels.title: Spans/s into Tempo
panels.description: Zero until an API image loads an OTel SDK; the pipeline is wired either way.

panels.title: Up by job
panels.description: TargetDown fires on any zero here for five minutes.

panels.title: Loki push requests
panels.description: Alloy and the Grafana datasource both go through this route.

panels.title: Server spans by service (span metrics)
panels.description: Tempo generates these from the traces it stores and remote-writes them into Prometheus.

panels.title: Alloy OTLP receiver
panels.description: Alloy's own counters for the OTLP receiver the APIs send traces and metrics to.

panels.title: Prometheus samples appended
panels.description: Scrapes plus the span metrics Tempo remote-writes.

panels.title: Firing alerts
panels.description: Every alert Prometheus is currently reporting to Alertmanager, which publishes it to the dev SNS topic.

panels.title: Alertmanager notifications
panels.description: sns is the only receiver on this box; the count is notifications handed to SNS, not emails delivered.
